issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for class Farm: the problem statement (and the starter Main) require and instantiate a no-argument constructor Farm(), but the solution implementation only provides a single-argument constructor public Farm(int initialCapacity). This discrepancy means code that uses new Farm() (as shown in the template Main and specified in the text "Initialize the ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments") will not compile against the provided solution and will confuse students about which constructor to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a public no-argument constructor to Farm that initializes the internal ArrayList (for example: public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }). You may also keep the existing Farm(int initialCapacity) overload, but ensure the no-arg constructor exists so it matches the problem specification and the example/template usage (new Farm()).
